A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A and B support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original steering experiments measuring token probabilities, concept presence, cross-entropy, and MMLU, plus UFM training results in Appendix B.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds experiments on additional concepts, limited steering data, layer sensitivity, and judge reliability.

M1.justification: The difference-of-means vector construction, additive residual-stream intervention, and token-position variants remain unchanged. Section 6 adds practical guidance for searching over steering strength, without replacing the analyzed or evaluated steering procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from eight steering concepts to twelve, adding math, coding, medical, and sycophancy. Table 1 and Figures A.18–A.21 document this substantial extension into topical domains. These are concept-steering evaluations, not new mathematical, coding, or medical accuracy benchmarks; FineWeb and MMLU remain.

E2.justification: No new competing steering algorithm is evaluated. Existing steering variants remain; the additional LLM judges are measurement-sensitivity controls rather than baselines competing with the steering method.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols using 10 positive and 10 negative prompts alongside the retained 500-per-set setup, denser layer sweeps, alternative judge models, and revised judge prompting. These substantially extend evaluation design; they do not establish changes to the retained main experiments.

E4.justification: New analyses test limited-data steering (Figures A.7–A.11), judge-model sensitivity (A.12–A.13), judge-prompt errors and corrections (A.14), and layer-dependent behavior (A.22–A.23). The original normalization, token-position, resampling, and contrastive-negative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure A.3 in both versions reports means and standard deviations over five runs resampling P and N. Both retain the stated omission of error bars from main figures; no new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice is reported.

E6.justification: The original main and matched appendix plots retain their results. v2 adds substantial results for new concepts, limited-data steering, layer sweeps, and judge sensitivity. Figures A.12–A.14 additionally show flat zero estimates from the base judge and changes in concept-presence curves following prompt refinement, rather than improved steering under an unchanged metric.

T1.justification: Proposition 4.1 adds a nonzero condition on steering-vector rows, and Appendix B.6 specifies the corresponding nonzero centered-direction condition for LayerNorm. Appendix B.1 removes special-case limit expansions while retaining the general formula. The principal UFM theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and three principal contributions retain their meaning. Section 6 newly claims that the existing theory can structure strength selection by restricting the search before degeneration and optimizing concept presence within a quality budget.

C2.justification: v2 adds judge false positives as an explanation for non-sigmoidal concept-presence curves and explains why continuous scoring alone may not resolve them (Appendix A.2.4). Section 3.2 also adds orthogonality versus representational entanglement as an explanation for differing off-target effects.

D1.justification: v2 supplies model layer counts in Table A.2, explicit configurations for new experiments, and the revised evil-concept judge prompt in Appendix A.2.4. The existing generation template, code-link disclosure, and cluster information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cheng et al. (2024) on adaptive activation control and Wehner et al. (2025) on representation engineering. These extend positioning around adaptive strength selection and entangled concepts; the broader related-work framing remains.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain recognizable. v2 subdivides Appendix A into setup and analysis sections, renames Section 4, edits language and proof explanations, and adds an impact statement and appendix content warning.

P2.justification: v2 adds extensive plot grids for limited-data tests, judges, new concepts, and layer sweeps. It moves and expands v1's token-example Table A.2 into main-text Table 1, adds an appendix figure-overview table, and labels vertical axes in Figures 6–7. Existing appendix plots are retained through renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves validation and transparency through broader concept coverage, limited-data tests, and an explicit audit of judge errors, while tightening normalization conditions. These strengthen the retained findings. However, Figures A.12–A.13 still show judge disagreements, the prompt correction addresses selected cases, and the strength-selection guidance remains unvalidated, supporting a limited overall quality gain.
